subject.title: Feature: Pre-compaction agent notification, structured handoff window, and deferral mechanism

question: Should OpenClaw add an agent-controlled pre-compaction lifecycle contract, and if so should it include warnings only, a structured handoff/checkpoint turn, bounded deferral, or some narrower subset?
rationale: The request crosses product UX, public config, persistence, and security boundaries because it can change when agents get extra write opportunities and whether compaction may be delayed after context pressure is detected.

options.title: Adopt warning and handoff only
options.body: Add a narrow opt-in warning plus structured handoff/checkpoint path while leaving agent-requested deferral out until authority semantics are settled.

options.title: Adopt full bounded deferral
options.body: Allow warning, handoff, and DEFER only with explicit max duration, audit trail, checkpoint matching, idempotency, and expiry rules.

options.title: Decline new lifecycle surface
options.body: Keep memoryFlush, notifyUser, hooks, and checkpoints as the supported compaction surfaces and route remaining needs to narrower follow-ups or plugins.

recommendation.title: Adopt warning and handoff only
recommendation.body: Add a narrow opt-in warning plus structured handoff/checkpoint path while leaving agent-requested deferral out until authority semantics are settled.

likelyOwner.reason: The memoryFlush implementation is the closest existing pre-compaction lifecycle behavior and is central to the requested handoff path.
